source: Chainlink secure development practices — own words
title: Missing freshness check on latestRoundData
mechanism: A protocol reads the Chainlink price with latestRoundData() but never checks updatedAt, so a frozen/stale feed continues to be trusted for borrow/liquidate/swap decisions.
root_cause: Staleness check missing on the feed result.
preconditions: price is used for a value-bearing decision
feed can go stale (heartbeat elapses)
no updatedAt guard
freshness_requirements: updatedAt must be within MAX_STALE (e.g. 3600s) of block.timestamp; answeredInRound >= roundId
invariant: no value-bearing decision uses a price older than MAX_STALE.
incorrect_behavior: a stale price (pre-move) is treated as current, over- or under-valuing positions.
exploit_sequence: feed goes stale at a favorable price
remediation: require(block.timestamp - updatedAt <= MAX_STALE) and sanity bounds; add a fallback feed.
verification_evidence: Chainlink docs; reproducible in Foundry with a mocked stale round.

title: Incorrect decimal normalization of feed price
mechanism: Chainlink feeds have fixed decimals per feed (e.g. 8 for USD pairs, 18 for ETH/USD on some feeds, 6 for some L2 feeds); a protocol that assumes 8 decimals (or hardcodes a scalar) computes prices 10^Nx too high/low, letting users borrow/withdraw at a wrong valuation.
root_cause: Hardcoded price-decimals assumption not matched to the actual feed decimals (and not corrected for token decimals).
preconditions: protocol assumes a fixed feed-decimals (e.g. 1e8)
the deployed feed has different decimals (e.g. 1e18, 1e6 on some L2s)
or token decimals differ from 18
freshness_requirements: freshness per the heartbeat (see stale case)
price_validation: must normalize feed decimals to the protocol's internal scale before use
invariant: price * amount computed with the correct 1e-X normalization for feed AND token decimals.
incorrect_behavior: a 1e6-decimals feed read as 1e8 inflates price 100x; 1e18 feed read as 1e8 deflates it 1e10x.
impact: Over-borrow / unfair withdrawal / direct value extraction.
remediation: Read feed.decimals() and token decimals, normalize both to a common scale; never hardcode.
code_evidence:
uint price = uint(feed.latestAnswer()); // assumes 8 decimals
uint value = amount * price / 1e8;
corrected_code:
uint8 fd = feed.decimals(); uint8 td = token.decimals();
uint value = amount * price * 10**(18 - td) / 10**(fd - 8) ... // scale both to 1e18
verification_evidence: Frequent C4 finding; reproduce by mocking a feed with non-8 decimals and asserting the wrong value.

source: public audit corpus — spot price dependence (Uniswap-style)
title: Spot-price dependence (Uniswap reserve ratio / slot0)
mechanism: A protocol prices assets with the raw Uniswap reserve ratio or slot0 (the current spot), which a single large swap moves in one transaction; flash-loanable manipulation breaks the valuation.
root_cause: Using instantaneous spot price without time-weighting or deviation protection.
preconditions: price read from pool spot (getReserves ratio or slot0)
pool liquidity is small relative to the attacker's capital
the price feeds a mint/borrow/liquidate decision in the same tx as the swap
freshness_requirements: none (spot is instantaneous) — this is the flaw
invariant: valuation must not be movable by a single transaction's swap (use TWAP + min liquidity).
incorrect_behavior: one swap moves the spot price used for the valuation, enabling arbitrage against the protocol.
remediation: Use Uniswap TWAP (observe() with min interval), enforce a minimum liquidity bound, and add deviation checks vs an external reference.
code_evidence: (uint r0, uint r1,) = pool.getReserves(); uint price = r0 * 1e18 / r1;
corrected_code:
(uint32[] memory ts, int56[] memory c,) = pool.observe([now - TWAP_WINDOW, now]);
uint price = UniswapV3Oracle.consult(pool, TWAP_WINDOW);
verification_evidence: Uniswap docs warning; reproducible with a single large swap in a Foundry fork test.

source: public audit corpus — TWAP manipulation on low liquidity
title: TWAP manipulation on low-liquidity pairs (short/zero window)
mechanism: A TWAP with a too-short window (or zero-liquidity accumulation) is nearly as manipulable as spot: the attacker moves the price for the window, the time-weighted average follows within tolerance, and the protocol prices against it.
root_cause: TWAP window too short relative to liquidity, or no minimum-liquidity requirement, making the average manipulable.
preconditions: TWAP window small (minutes) or accumulation empty
pool liquidity low relative to attacker capital
value-bearing logic uses the TWAP
invariant: the TWAP must not be movable by capital of a realistic attacker within one window.
incorrect_behavior: a short window TWAP follows the manipulated spot almost 1:1.
exploit_sequence: move the spot price (one large swap)
hold/move for the TWAP window (few blocks on a short window)
price the protocol's conversion at the moved average
impact: Same class as spot dependence; value extraction via mint/borrow/liquidate.
remediation: Use a long TWAP window, require minimum liquidity, and cap the price move per window (deviation check vs a second oracle).
code_evidence: uint price = UniswapV2Library.quote(...); // or v3 consult with 60s window
corrected_code: uint price = v3Oracle.consult(pool, 1800); // >= 30 min + require(pool.liquidity > MIN)
verification_evidence: Audit pattern; reproducible by simulating a window-length price move in Foundry.

title: Missing sequencer-upkeep check on L2 feeds
mechanism: On L2s (Arbitrum/Base/OP), when the sequencer is down, feeds freeze at their last value; a protocol that does not check SequencerUptimeFeed keeps pricing against frozen data during an outage (stale-equivalent).
root_cause: Missing check of the L2 sequencer-uptime feed before trusting prices during outages.
preconditions: deployed on an L2 with a SequencerUptimeFeed
price feed can freeze while sequencer is down
no uptime check before value-bearing reads
freshness_requirements: sequencer must be up; grace period elapsed
price_validation: uptime feed: isUp() true and (startedAt + GRACE) <= now
invariant: no protocol price is read while the L2 sequencer is down.
incorrect_behavior: during a sequencer outage the frozen price is used, enabling stale-price arbitrage.
exploit_sequence: wait for/observe a sequencer outage window
impact: Bad debt / unfair liquidations during outages.
remediation: Check SequencerUptimeFeed (isUp && grace period) on every value-bearing read on L2s.
code_evidence: (, int price, , , ) = feed.latestRoundData(); use(price); // no uptime check
verification_evidence: Chainlink docs; reproducible by mocking SequencerUptimeFeed down.

source: public audit corpus — incorrect feed configuration
title: Incorrect price-feed configuration (proxy vs deviation / wrong pair)
mechanism: The wrong feed is wired for an asset (e.g. a USD feed used as USD-per-token, or a deprecated proxy, or an asset feed that is pegged while the real asset trades differently), so valuations are wrong even with fresh data.
root_cause: Feed address/pair/decimals misconfiguration at deploy or governance.
preconditions: feed maps to the wrong pair (inverted, pegged, different asset)
or proxy deprecated / points to a stale aggregator
no sanity/deviation check against expected value range
price_validation: sanity range / cross-check against a second source
invariant: the configured feed must quote the intended asset in the intended quote and direction.
incorrect_behavior: borrow/liquidate uses a wrong or pegged price, under- or over-valuing positions.
exploit_sequence: (misconfig) borrow against an overvalued asset / liquidate an undervalued one
impact: Systematic mispricing; unfair liquidations or bad debt.
remediation: Validate feed pair+decimals at deploy; add deviation/sanity bounds; test with live feed addresses.
corrected_code:
require(feed.decimals() == 8, 'dec'); // + verify pair in an allowlist at deploy
// + require(price within [MIN, MAX] sanity band)
verification_evidence: C4 misconfiguration findings; check feed.decimals() and compare against a reference on-chain.

source: public audit corpus — fallback oracle logic
title: Incorrect fallback-oracle logic (fallback to more manipulable source)
mechanism: When the primary feed fails, a protocol falls back to a more manipulable source (e.g. an in-protocol spot/twap or a self-reported price), and the fallback is not bounded — so an attacker triggers the fallback and manipulates the price.
root_cause: Fallback oracle lacks the manipulation resistance of the primary, or the failover condition is attacker-triggerable.
preconditions: fallback path exists when primary feed errors/returns 0
fallback source is manipulable (spot/self-reported)
attacker can trigger the failover condition
freshness_requirements: primary freshness; fallback must add manipulation resistance
price_validation: fallback bounded by deviation vs primary's last good value
invariant: a failover must never downgrade price manipulation resistance.
incorrect_behavior: the fallback accepts a manipulable value the primary would reject.
exploit_sequence: make the primary feed revert/return 0 (or wait for it)
protocol falls back to the manipulable source
impact: Direct value extraction via downgraded oracle path.
remediation: Keep the fallback manipulation-resistant, bound it by deviation vs the last good primary value, and never let an attacker trigger failover cheaply.
code_evidence: try feed.latestRoundData() returns (p) { use p } catch { use getSpotPrice(); } // fallback unguarded
corrected_code: catch { require(now - lastGoodAt <= WINDOW); p = lastGood; } // or TWAP + deviation bound vs lastGood
verification_evidence: Audit finding class; reproduce by forcing the primary to revert and manipulating the fallback in Foundry.

title: Cross-oracle inconsistency (different sources diverge)
mechanism: A protocol reads the same asset from multiple oracles (different feeds, aggregators, or TWAP windows) for different decisions (collateral vs debt vs liquidation), and their divergence is not reconciled — an attacker arbitrages the gap between the two prices.
root_cause: Multiple independent price sources used without a consistency/deviation check between them.
preconditions: collateral and debt priced from different feeds/sources
the two sources can diverge (stale one, different pair, different windows)
no cross-source deviation guard
invariant: the prices used for related decisions must agree within a deviation bound.
incorrect_behavior: a stale/divergent source underprices one side, enabling borrow-then-default or unfair liquidation.
exploit_sequence: find/induce divergence between the two sources (one stale)
borrow against the higher collateral price, repay at the lower debt price
impact: Arbitrage value extraction; bad debt accumulation.
remediation: Reconcile multi-source prices with a deviation check and use a single source of truth per asset where possible.
code_evidence: uint pc = collateralFeed.get(); uint pd = debtFeed.get(); // no cross check
corrected_code:
require(withinDeviation(pc, pd, MAX_DEV), 'oracle divergence');
useMedian(pc, pd);
verification_evidence: Audit finding; reproduce by mocking two diverging feeds in Foundry.
